query_text: what does the word comet mean

content.text:
The word **"comet"** has an interesting etymological history:

## Definition
A **comet** is a small icy body in space that, when it travels close to the Sun, heats up and releases gases and dust, forming a bright glowing "tail" that can be visible from Earth.

## Etymology (Word Origin)
The word **"comet"** comes from:
- **Latin**: *cometa* or *cometes*
- **Ancient Greek**: *κομήτης (komētēs)*, meaning **"long-haired"** or **"wearing long hair"**
- Derived from the Greek word *κόμη (komē)*, meaning **"hair of the head"**

The name was given because ancient Greek and Roman astronomers thought the bright, flowing tail of a comet resembled **long, flowing hair** streaming behind it. The full Greek phrase used was **"ἀστήρ κομήτης" (astēr komētēs)**, meaning **"long-haired star."**

## In Summary
| Language | Word | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| English | Comet | A space body with a glowing tail |
| Latin | *Cometa* | Long-haired |
| Greek | *Komētēs* | Long-haired / Wearing long hair |
| Greek root | *Komē* | Hair of the head |

So essentially, when you say the word **"comet,"** you're using an ancient Greek description of what they saw — a **"hairy star"** — because of its brilliant, hair-like tail! 🌠
